title: Adaptive token-window admission controller with speculative micro-batch compaction
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a tenant-aware admission controller for the real-time console metrics pipeline that enforces per-tenant token budgets using a sliding time window and performs speculative micro-batch compaction to improve throughput without violating latency SLOs. The controller lives at the ingress gateway (edge proxy) and as a local admission agent on each ingest worker to provide fast rejects and graceful degradation.

Problem statement:
We see bursts from a small fraction of tenants (hot tenants / spikes from integration tests) that cause large increases in per-tenant queue lengths, increased batching delays, and 99.9th percentile latency violations for other tenants. Existing global throttlers operate at coarse granularity and either overreject or allow noisy neighbors to monopolize shared runners. We need a finer-grained, latency-aware mechanism that: (1) caps token/time consumption per tenant, (2) prioritizes low-latency traffic and control-plane events, and (3) compacts speculative micro-batches when safe to improve overall token throughput.

Goals:
- Enforce soft and hard token budgets per tenant using a sliding token-window (configurable window length and token budget).
- Admit requests greedily when headroom exists; when near budget, allow speculative micro-batches that compact small requests into a single inference batch only if compaction keeps expected tail latency under configured SLO.
- Provide local fast path for accepts/rejects (probabilistic admission) to avoid extra RPC latency to central controller under high load.
- Emit detailed telemetry for debugging and automated rollback: admitted_rate, rejected_rate, microbatch_compaction_rate, avg_batch_size, burst_fill, tail_latency_99.9, queue_depth_percentile, reservoir_evictions.

Design overview:
- Token budget model: each tenant has a token_budget per window (default 100k tokens / 60s window). Tokens consumed = estimate(tokens for request) + queued_tokens. Window implemented as fixed-size ring of subwindows for O(1) updates.
- Admission prioritization: requests classified into priority bands (control, interactive-low, batch-bg) based on route headers. Higher-priority requests can preempt queued BG batches up to a configurable preemption limit.
- Speculative micro-batch compaction: when two or more small requests from same or compatible tenants arrive within a short coalescing window (e.g., 5ms), attempt to compact into one micro-batch at the local worker. Compaction is speculative: it proceeds only if predicted tail latency (local model) remains below tenant_slo_tail. If prediction fails, we fallback to emitting the smaller batch or split.
- Local vs central controller: a central quota store (fast in-memory replication) holds global long-term budgets and policy; local admission agents maintain a soft shadow copy and make fast accept/reject decisions. Central controller periodically reconciles and issues backpressure hints.
- Backpressure signals: expose a lightweight HTTP/GRPC hint API between gateway and workers. Gateway can mark routes as throttled and emit x-backpressure headers for downstream clients.

Implementation plan (phased):
1) PoC (2 wks): implement sliding token window library and local admission agent with config knobs. Add unit tests and microbench harness to validate correctness and perf.
2) Microbatch compaction prototype (2 wks): implement local compaction logic with simple latency predictor (moving percentile over recent batches). Add toggle via feature flag.
3) Integration + metrics (1 wk): wire telemetry through statsd/observability pipeline and add Grafana dashboard templates + alert rules (SLO breach if rejected_rate > 1% && tail_latency_99.9 > configured).
4) Canary rollout (2 wks): enable for 5% tenants, monitor impact, iterate on predictor and window sizing.
5) Full rollout + docs (1 wk): update runbooks, SDK docs for backpressure headers.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New metrics (per-tenant and aggregated): admitted_rate, rejected_rate, microbatch_compaction_attempts, microbatch_compaction_successes, avg_microbatch_size, tokens_consumed_window, window_fill_percentile, tail_latency_99.9_by_priority.
- Dashboards: "Admission Controller Overview", "Hot-tenant Investigations", "Compaction Efficacy" with drilldowns by tenant and route.
- Alerts: token_budget_exhaustion (high), compaction_fallback_rate (medium), admission_reject_spike (high).

Rollout & Safeguards:
- Feature-flagged per-environment and per-tenant. Default to disabled for Dedicated & Private till validated.
- Soft mode: controller will log but not reject until an analyst promotes the tenant.
- Kill-switch: global env var to disable admission controller instantly.
- Metrics-driven rollback: automated rollback if reject_rate > 5% or target-tail latency increases > 10% for > 10 minutes.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for sliding window correctness and token accounting.
- Load tests with synthetic hot-tenant bursts using existing ingest harness. Evaluate percentiles and compaction effect on tokens/throughput.
- Chaos tests: simulate central controller partition and verify local agents continue to operate safely.
- Security: ensure backpressure hints cannot be spoofed; authenticate gateway <-> worker RPC with mTLS.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should token budget be in tokens or an abstract CPU/IO weight? Tokens map well to downstream cost but may not capture all resource contention.
- Predictor complexity: simple moving-percentile is cheap and stable but may underreact to sudden shifts; ML-based predictor could be better but increases flakiness.
- Cross-tenant compaction: we currently allow compaction across tenants only for low-sensitivity routes to avoid mixing data in traces; this needs policy.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.internal/redwood/ingest/token-window-admission (draft)
- PoC branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4212 (WIP)
- Dashboard proto: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/abc123/admission-controller
- Load test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-load-tests

Acceptance criteria:
- Local agent enforces sliding window correctly in unit tests and small-scale load tests.
- Speculative micro-batch compaction improves average batch size by >=15% for small requests without increasing tail latency >5%.
- Canary tenants show no regression in 99.9th latency for interactive-high routes.
- Observability surfaces all new metrics and runbook exists for investigation.

Longer-term improvements (future epics):
- Global adaptive policies that learn per-tenant budgets automatically from usage patterns.
- Integrate cost-aware admission to minimize cloud GPU spend under heavy load.
- Tighten compaction model with a learned latency predictor and per-model profiles.
